parts.text: In this experiment, you are to make two sets of measurements as accurately as you can in order to determine the density of glass. Carry out the following instructions referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1 Method 1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Use the two blocks of wood and the rule to measure the external diameter d of the test- tube in cm. d = ......................................................... cm

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Draw a labelled diagram to show how you used the blocks of wood and the rule to find, as accurately as possible, a value for the external diameter of the test-tube.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the external volume V e of the test-tube using the equation V e = π d 2 h 4 . V e = ............................................................... [3]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Use the balance provided to measure the mass m 1 of the test-tube. m 1 = .......................................................... [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Completely fill the test-tube with water. Pour the water into the measuring cylinder and record the volume V i of the water. V i = ...............................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the density ρ of the glass using the equation ρ = m 1 ( V e – V i ) . ρ = ............................................................... [1] Method 2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) Pour water into the measuring cylinder up to about the 175 cm 3 mark. Record this volume V 1 . V 1 = ...............................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Carefully lower the test-tube, open end uppermost, into the measuring cylinder so that it floats. Record the new volume reading V 2 from the measuring cylinder. V 2 = ...............................................................

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the mass m 2 of the test-tube using the equation m 2 = k ( V 2 – V 1 ) where k = 1.0 g/cm 3 . m 2 = ............................................................... [3]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) Use the wooden rod to push the test-tube, open end uppermost, down to the bottom of the measuring cylinder so that the test-tube is full of water and below the surface. Remove the wooden rod. Record the new volume reading V 3 from the measuring cylinder. V 3 = ...............................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the density ρ of the glass using the equation ρ = m 2 ( V 3 – V 1 ) . ρ = ............................................................... [2]
